transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2027-05-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes (target)
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Jamal (Redwood SE), Amina (CISO, Lyra), Liam (Head Infra), Maya (Legal), Ravi (Platform)

Summary:
Quick security & compliance review focusing on data residency, region pinning, KMS/customer-managed keys, and subprocessor footprints. Lyra wants strict EU-only processing for a subset of patient data, audit log retention details, and clarity on SSO/RBAC integration for cross-team access. Redwood outlined Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and proposed a key-splitting KMS approach and routing fallbacks.

Topics:
- EU-only route enforcement and how Redwood handles routing and fallbacks
- Customer-managed KMS options, per-region keying, and KMS escrow
- Subprocessor inventory & contractual controls; what triggers data export to US
- Audit logging retention, access logs, and SIEM integration
- RBAC/SSO (SAML/OIDC) and scoped roles for model access and cost telemetry

Transcript body (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh we'll run about an hour. quick intro — i'm Sofia, i'm the AE on the account, with Jamal our solutions engineer.
[00:14] Amina (Lyra CISO): Thanks Sofia. We want to focus on region locking and what actually leaves the EU for our clinical workflows. High level first then we can dig into keys and logs.
[00:27] Jamal (Redwood SE): Great. we'll start with routing — Redwood's platform supports policy-based routing. for EU-only requests you can set a route that pins to the eu cluster, and we can enforce a hard deny if no eu capacity is available or optionally fail-open to a lower-tier model in same region.
[00:42] Liam (Head Infra): pause — when you say "eu cluster" is that a logical routing tag in the control plane or physically separate infra with separate tenancy? we need to know whether there's a possibility of cross-border memory spill or kv cache replication.
[00:58] Jamal (Redwood SE): good question. it's physical separation at the serving layer — compute and storage are in EU regions. the control plane still runs in Redwood's control region but metadata-only; payloads for pinned routes do not leave the EU serving fabric. K V cache replication is disabled for eu-pinned tenants so there's no cross-region kv cache replication.
[01:20] Amina: ok that helps, but we need to see the network diagram and proof — subprocessor list and where each one operates.
[01:26] Sofia: absolutely, we'll attach the subprocessor inventory by region. Jamal will walk through the KMS options.
[01:33] Jamal: on KMS, we support three patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys (default), 2) customer-managed keys in the cloud KMS (bring-your-own-key), and 3) hybrid where we keep per-region keys and support escrow. for EU-only processing you can bring your own KMS keys in the EU region.
[01:52] Ravi (Platform): by "per-region keys" do you mean separate CMKs per region or a single key with geographic restrictions? we want strict separation — no key material leaving the EU.
[02:03] Jamal: separate CMKs per region. the keys are created in the customer's project/account and we reference them via key alias. Redwood never receives raw key material. we do support hardware-backed keys (HSM).
[02:16] Maya (Legal): what's the mechanism for key rotation and do you support split-key escrow in case of customer lockout? also curious about key custody during incident support.
[02:27] Jamal: rotation is fan-out through KMS API; Redwood doesn't hold private key components. for escrow we can support a multi-party approach — e.g., keys split between customer KMS and escrow managed by a neutral third-party. it's not out-of-the-box but we can design it for enterprise Private deployments.
[02:45] Amina: and audit logs — retention, schema, who can access them? we need immutable logs for 7 years for some clinical audits.
[02:55] Sofia: Redwood Console has audit and token-level traces. we can export audit logs to your SIEM or S3 in the EU. retention is configurable; default is 180 days, enterprise retention options available.
[03:12] Liam: is the export synchronous or do you push batches? what's latency and are there guarantees about log delivery to our bucket?
[03:20] Jamal: logs are delivered asynchronously in near-real-time. we provide delivery promises as part of Dedicated/Private SLAs. for Hosted customers we offer a best-effort delivery and a delivery retry policy. we can discuss guaranteed delivery and proofs in the contract.
[03:39] Ravi: any PII redaction at the log level? patient identifiers should not be present in cleartext in Redwood's logs.
[03:47] Jamal: by default metadata and request headers are logged; we'll implement structured masking rules for PII. for EU-only tenants we can configure full payload exclusion from Redwood-managed logs and only keep hashes or redacted fields, and push full logs to your S3 in EU under your KMS.
[04:06] Maya: what about subprocessor communication — who do you share logs or backups with? we need contractual assurances.
[04:13] Sofia: we'll include subprocessors and their regions in the inventory. subprocessors only get data if necessary for service operation; for EU-only pinned accounts subprocessors with non-eu hosting will be blocked unless explicitly approved and the data is redacted.
[04:30] Amina: okay, fallback behavior — suppose EU region is under capacity during a spike, how does Redwood handle requests? we cannot have data leave EU.
[04:39] Jamal: you can choose a strict enforcement mode (requests fail with 429/451), or you can choose an allowed fallback to another EU region or to a lower-capacity model in EU. falling back to US is an option but would only be used if you opt in; it's not the default for pinned accounts.
[04:58] Liam: so default is fail closed. good. can we get an SLA clause to that effect?
[05:02] Sofia: yes, for Dedicated/Private we can put region availability SLOs in the order form.
[05:08] Amina: SSO — we use SAML with our IdP, and we need SCIM + role-based controls scoped to projects. can we map RBAC in Redwood to our internal roles?
[05:18] Jamal: we support SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and role mappings. you can create scoped roles (model-runner, viewer, admin) and bind them to your groups. audit hooks will show who executed each call.
[05:31] Ravi: one more infra question — encryption at rest for temporary KV caches used during generation, is that encrypted with the region CMK? and what's lifetime of ephemeral artifacts?
[05:41] Jamal: ephemeral artifacts are encrypted at rest with the region CMK. lifetime is configurable; default TTL is 48 hours but we can reduce that for EU-only datasets. ephemeral keys are rotated frequently; we do not persist raw cache content beyond TTL.
[05:57] Maya: legal wants to know if Redwood has any cross-border subprocessors performing model fine-tuning or evals that might pull EU data to US for research.
[06:07] Sofia: Redwood does not perform customer data-based model training without explicit consent. our verification processes require a signed agreement for any training work. subprocessors used for analytics are region-tagged and we can exclude those from EU-only customers.
[06:20] Amina: great. we may ask for a controlled pilot with a small dataset and tight logging to validate all these assumptions.
[06:25] Sofia: that makes sense. Jamal, can we propose a pilot plan?
[06:28] Jamal: yes, propose a 2-week pilot: 1) configure EU-pinned route, 2) configure BYOK (EU CMK), 3) run a small batch of synthetic requests, 4) validate audit logs and SIEM export. We'll provide a test plan and runbook.
[06:45] Liam: what's the expected lead time to get dedicated EU capacity? if we want strict isolation we'd prefer Dedicated or Private.
[06:52] Sofia: Dedicated has a procurement lead time — typically 4–6 weeks depending on capacity. Private (on-prem or VPC) is longer. For pilot we can do Hosted EU-pinned with BYOK.
[07:05] Maya: contractually, we need subprocessors enumerated and a clause that disallows any cross-border processing without prior written consent.
[07:12] Sofia: we can include that in the DPA for EU-only accounts; we'll share a proposed clause.
[07:18] Amina: last question — can you show us an example of the audit event schema and an example log with redaction?
[07:25] Jamal: yes we have examples. i'll attach a sample json event (note: PII redacted).
[07:31] Ravi: will you also include the network diagram and KMS key stitching docs?
[07:34] Jamal: yes. we'll send the infra diagram, the KMS options matrix, and the region routing playbook.
[07:41] Sofia: sounds good. i'll follow up with the SOC2, ISO attestation, and the subprocessor map.
[07:46] Amina: thanks all. appreciate the clarity.
[07:49] Sofia: quick recap and next steps — we'll circulate docs and set a follow-up for 1 week out to confirm pilot scope. any final comments?
[07:58] Maya: none from legal, thanks.
[08:00] Meeting ends (wrap-up and action item confirmations).
